interface.stateModel: MatterRevisions carries one matter-shared sourceVersion and a per-target append-only revision list with its own head; every transition takes the state and returns a new state, and a refusal returns the input state by reference.
interface.purity: No storage, no clock, no ambient IDs. IDs and timestamps come from an injected RevisionContext, so the same state, command and context always produce the same result.
interface.ownership: The module never stores an AST, entries array or figure set it was handed. saveRevision, restoreRevision and adoptInputs each store a structural copy, so an editor mutating its working AST cannot rewrite a revision that already exists.
interface.astBoundary: The AST is opaque to this module. The caller passes a contract-validated AST and its astHash; draftAstSchema stays the single source of AST validity in packages/contracts.

acceptance.observed: 15 tests passed; 0 failed, 0 skipped. Saving a revision on target A leaves target B's revision list, head and figure set deep-equal to their pre-call value, advances only target A's head, sets parentId to the previous head and leaves the matter sourceVersion unchanged. The revisions produced by all three commands that create one — saveRevision, restoreRevision and adoptInputs — are parsed against the frozen draftRevisionSchema, snapshotRefSchema and draftInputRefSchema, the restore's figure set is parsed against figureSetRevisionSchema, and each target keeps its own parent chain.

A base that is no longer the target head is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and latestRevisionId, and the refusal returns the input state by reference so nothing is appended, reordered or rewritten. Unknown targets, archived targets and revisions of another target are refused with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND or INVALID_TRANSITION without a write. switchTargetView returns the identical state object, so a view change cannot bump a version. Restoring the first revision while a later revision is the target head creates a new revision with restoredFrom set to that first revision and a copied (non-aliased) AST; a contract-valid full_read confirmation bound to that first revision is current when it is made, is not current once a later revision exists, and is not current again after the restore, so the old approval is never revived. restore_bound creates a real figure set revision (validated against figureSetRevisionSchema, parentId = the previous set, entries copied, previous set retained) and refuses with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND when the set the draft was written against is no longer retained; keep_current creates no set and reports figureMismatch. A restored revision keeps its own input sourceVersion and isInputStale then reports true against the current input. adoptInputs is refused with INVALID_INPUT unless acknowledgedInputReview is true and, from a stale base, with VERSION_CONFLICT; an input pointing past the matter sourceVersion is refused with INPUT_STALE. On a draft whose summary is five AI paragraphs with five ai_paragraph confirmations, one edit returns all five to pending: every confirmation is current on the generated revision and none is current after the edit.

acceptance.command: npm run test:v6 -- V6-04; npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present; npm test --workspaces --if-present
acceptance.observed: The same state, command and freshly seeded context produce a deep-equal revision and next state on both runs, and a deep-frozen input state is unchanged afterwards. A refused command returns the same state reference and an identical error. A saved revision stores its own copy of the AST, so mutating the submitted object after the call leaves the revision and the returned state unchanged. Workspace typecheck and all workspace tests exit 0. These checks cover a pure state transition, not persisted refresh or retry behavior, because this ticket writes no storage.

specAcceptance.reason: Locked-section redaction is a preview read path with no implementation in this ticket; V6-04 only transitions draft revisions.
Risk anchoring and anchor redaction are preview and risk read behavior, not revision state.

The suite builds a draft whose summary holds five AI paragraphs, records five contract-valid ai_paragraph confirmations on the generated revision, then saves one edit and asserts all five are no longer current. The confirmations are contract-valid records rather than rows in a confirmation store, because this ticket creates no such store; the reset itself is shown.

A save or adopt whose base revision is no longer the target head is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT plus latestRevisionId, and no state changes; the buffer and the merge view are UI behavior outside this module.

restoreRevision copies the earlier draft into a new revision with restoredFrom set, a new id, an unaliased AST copy and no inherited confirmation or approval; restore_bound appends a real FigureSetRevision over the restored draft's own entries and keep_current keeps the current set and reports the mismatch.

adoptInputs rejects the command with INVALID_INPUT when acknowledgedInputReview is false and creates an adopted_inputs revision bound to the current input when it is true; the new revision id means no confirmation carries over.
The expert-escalation path creates a service order and is outside the revision domain module.
INVALID_AST for a claim depending on a later claim is enforced by draftAstSchema in packages/contracts and was verified by V6-03; V6-04 treats the AST as an opaque, already-validated value.
The local-preview label and the absent payment button are UI behavior with no revision transition.

limitations: Preservation could not be re-verified in this isolated worktree: the V6-01 baseline untracked manifest describes 407 paths of the user's working checkout, none of which exist in a fresh worktree, and the worktree isolation hook refuses commands that target the original checkout. qa/v6/evidence/V6-04/scope.txt records the complete worktree delta instead: one modified shared barrel, the V6-04 write set, the two .planning files the orchestrator maintains for this plan, and the untracked node_modules symlink used as a local test-dependency mount. No other tracked or untracked file was touched.

The module imports nothing from packages/contracts. A cross-package dependency cannot be declared here because package-lock.json cannot be regenerated (npm install --package-lock-only fails at baseline with 404 for @patent/vibescanner-core). SnapshotRef and DraftInputRef are therefore declared structurally and drift is caught by the V6-04-A01 contract-validation test, which parses the produced revision against draftRevisionSchema, snapshotRefSchema and draftInputRefSchema.

S05-A03 is verified at the snapshot level: the suite builds a contract-valid full_read Confirmation bound to the pre-edit snapshot and shows it is no longer current after a save. Creating, listing and revoking confirmations belongs to V6-05.
No deployment, network call, model call, charge or real customer material was used. All fixtures are the deterministic synthetic set from packages/contracts/src/fixtures.ts.

decisionsRecorded.decision: V6-04 keeps the draft AST opaque and free of a packages/contracts dependency. AST validity stays with draftAstSchema in V6-03; V6-04 owns ordering, parents, staleness and figure binding, and its output is contract-validated in the suite.
A refused command returns the input state object itself rather than a copy, so a caller cannot accidentally persist a partially applied transition and a test can assert the refusal wrote nothing.
